verdict.rationale: Visa's Trusted Agent Protocol (the agent-trust layer) is genuinely published in the open — a public GitHub repo with a runnable reference implementation, documented RFC 9421 signature spec, and keyless access confirmed by a live probe (visa-ic-probe-rt-1, visa-intelligent-commerce-gh-1..5, visa-intelligent-commerce-docs-11). However, the actual Visa Intelligent Commerce payment protocol/API (the core 'commerce protocol' being enrolled/instructions/credentials REST calls) is not a freely readable open spec but a proprietary API gated behind a sandbox signup requiring organization details and 'terms acceptance' before test transactions (visa-ic-supp-10), and production access requires contacting Visa for fees (visa-ic-supp-8) — i.e., signing something is required to actually use the core protocol. Missing for 10: explicit version numbers for the published spec, evidence the core VIC payment API/spec (not just TAP) can be read and implemented with zero registration or terms acceptance, and independent corroboration beyond Visa's own docs/repo.
